brief: The Market Ear argues a Russell 2000 short-squeeze setup is building. The US 10-year has stalled near the same level as five sessions earlier despite feeling like it kept rising, yet bond vol kept pushing higher, raising the question of whether vol stress is overshooting the actual rate move; a reversal lower in rates could unwind that vol quickly and amplify the move. Technically, the 10-year could retrace to its 21-day MA at 5.08% for modest relief, or to the 50-day MA at 4.87% for a much larger move. Meanwhile Russell has started outperforming the S&P 500 after three months of underperformance, reclaiming its 200-day MA and testing a break above the downtrend channel in place since mid-August. Goldman Sachs data cited in the piece shows Russell 2000 positioning washed out: systematic exposure in just the 7th percentile and leveraged funds carrying record CFTC-tracked shorts. The note's thesis is that rates do not need to fall, only pause, to ignite the squeeze; an actual decline in rates would amplify it further.
